description:
We're a team of CS & ECE students who work hard. Our goal is to create informative space mission design game.

Some of our interests combined: 

astronomy, cosmology, gaming, electric circuits, hardware design, programming, quantum, control systems, instrumentation.
summary: There isn't a well known space game that is both educational, accurate and is fun to play. LEAP is a browser game that aims to address this challenge where you run a space company and take contracts to design real missions, from Explorer 1 in 1958 to the Moon landing and Artemis. You build a Site, make Parts, take a Contract, design the Spacecraft part by part, pick a rocket and launch site, and fly it.  After each flight the Mission Report explains why the Mission worked or failed, and Real History cards tell what happened on the real mission. It lets player players run a whole mission from objective to operation, fail safely and try again. It matters because these trade-offs usually stay abstract for students and this abstraction discourage students and players from learning and exploring, and going into the space as a domain of interest considering it as too hard to understand or boring.
details:
LEAP is a space company builder game where players develop a company and design, launch and fly Missions. The Eras follow real history, from Explorer 1 in 1958 to the Artemis missions till 2028. We also have a freeplay mode that doesn't follow anything.


The game is mainly targeted for players aged 12-15, and should use explorer mode (shows bars, words and pictures instead of numbers). While, Mission Director mode is for 16+ years old (shows every number and unit and has more complex minigames).

The Mission Designer shows six live bars for Mass, Power, Budget, Data, Communications and Time. The Launch planner groups the Mission under NASA's four mission Segments: User, Space, Ground and Launch. A free Test Run shows the chance of success before money is spent. The Launch is shown in 3D. Anomalies such as a stuck solar panel or an eclipse are short mini-games caused by the design's weak points. The game also contains a separate minigame section in the main menu for each of the targeted age group that teaches specific facts to the players. The Mission Report says what worked and why, using the design's own numbers. Real launch weather from NASA POWER can delay a Launch, and the location of the launchpad at each launch site changes what a rocket can lift.

Most of the tycoon games available around are city builders or parks (Cities Skylines, SimCity, and Roller-Coaster Tycoon), and we rarely see ones applied to other domains. Our game combines the fun of the tycoon games with historical story and space exploration, while keeping it educational and allowing the player to grasp the abstract design challenges faced by space companies while not needing to study rocket science or aerospace engineering and promotes space education worldwide.

Tools: TypeScript, Vite, three.js, HTML and CSS for coding the game, Python scripts prepare the NASA data. Blender for creating the 3D assets. Claude code, Gemini Lyria 3.5 for music, ChatGPT codex and chat as tools for writing the code and generating the images.

We chose it to be a browser based game so it can run on any operating system. We also included a .bat, .sh, .command files that installs all dependencies and open the game and make sure nothing is missing, so that people who are not deep in tech can install it and run the game.
